title: CQRV hardware target, schema v1.0.0
description: PHASE2_SPEC §C.1 (Stage 24a, Track C); report §3.1.3 (hardware profiles as a change of base), §5.3 (the trust boundary). A `HardwareTarget` extracted by the untrusted `hw/target.py` from a Qiskit fake backend and read by `cqr hw capabilities` (CQRV.Hardware.Target, Physlib-free). Every capability flag and every calibration group says where it came from (a `source` string). The file is written in the canonical form (keys sorted by code point, no whitespace, a trailing newline); every number inside `calibration` is a decimal string (Python's repr of the float the source gives), so that `snapshot.hash` — SHA3-256 of the canonical JSON of `calibration` — is computed identically by Python's hashlib and by Lean on the parsed object. Entries whose source gives no value are omitted; a missing mid-circuit measurement error is null with a note, and the readout error is never substituted for it. Figures are a snapshot of fake-backend data, not a device measurement: nothing here is 'verified on hardware'.

decimal.description: A finite decimal as Python's repr prints a float: 0.0001, 8e-05, 35.55555555555556.

perTupleNumber.description: Keyed by the comma-separated qubit tuple; values are JSON numbers (not hashed).

source.description: The fake backend's class and the package versions it was read with.

variant.description: Present on a hand-made variant: which flag was changed and why.

basis_gates.description: The native gate names (the target's operations that are Gates), sorted.

calibration.description: The snapshot that is hashed. All values are decimal strings.

t1_s.description: T1 per qubit, in seconds as the source gives it.

t2_s.description: T2 per qubit, in seconds as the source gives it.

timestamp.description: The timestamp the source gives for its calibration data.

hash.description: SHA3-256 hex digest of the canonical JSON of `calibration`.
